en: To be the explanation or reason for something; or to form a particular part of a total.
ex: How do you account for the sudden drop in sales?
你如何解釋銷量突然下降？

en: To get something, especially with some effort; or to visit a place for a short time.
ex: Good jobs are hard to come by these days.
現在好工作很難找。

en: To get as much advantage as possible from a situation that is not perfect.
ph: make the best of a bad situation
在糟糕情況下盡力而為
col: make the best of the weather
ex: We made the best of the rainy weather by staying in.
我們待在室內，把雨天過得很充實。

en: To provide something such as food or transport; or to apply a layer of something such as paint.
ph: lay on a coat of paint
ex: The hotel laid on a special dinner for us.
飯店為我們準備了特別的晚餐。

en: To not reach a required or expected standard or amount.
ex: The team fell short of its goal.
球隊未達成目標。

en: Over the whole of a person's body.
col: from head to toe in black
ex: She was covered in mud from head to toe.
她全身上下都沾滿了泥巴。

en: To begin a journey; or to start something in a particular way.
ph: start off on the right foot
ex: Let's start off with a quick game.
我們先玩個小遊戲開場吧。

en: To reduce the amount or size of something; or to cause a tree to fall by cutting.
ex: You should cut down on fast food.
你應該少吃速食。

en: To stop hoping or trying because you feel discouraged.
ex: Don't lose heart; try again.
別灰心，再試一次。

en: To realize that someone is lying or pretending; or to help someone get through a difficult time; or to stay with a task until finished.
ex: I could see through his excuses.
我看穿了他的藉口。

en: To agree with someone or something; or to accompany someone.
ex: I don't go along with his opinion.
我不贊同他的意見。

en: To send out a smell, heat, light or gas.
ex: The old fridge gives off a strange smell.
那台舊冰箱散發出奇怪的味道。

en: To reduce the amount or level of something; or to cause someone or something to fall.
ex: The new policy brought down unemployment.
新政策使失業率下降。

en: To need something; or to demand something; or to go and collect someone or something.
ex: This situation calls for careful thought.
這種情況需要仔細考慮。

en: To continue for longer than expected; or to keep talking for a long time.
ex: The meeting ran on for hours.
會議持續了好幾個小時。

en: To move to one side; or to avoid someone or something.
ex: He turned aside to avoid meeting her gaze.
他轉過身避開她的目光。

en: To visit someone for a short time, usually without planning.
col: drop in on your way home
ex: I'll drop in on you tomorrow evening.
我明天傍晚順道去看你。

en: To prevent someone or something from moving forward; or to keep information secret; or to stop yourself from showing a feeling.
ex: She couldn't hold back her tears.
她無法忍住眼淚。

en: To expect something to always be available and not feel thankful for it; or to believe something is true without checking.
ex: Don't take your family for granted.
別把你的家人視為理所當然。

en: To grab something suddenly and hold it firmly.
ex: She caught hold of the railing to stay steady.
她抓住欄杆以站穩。

en: To see or hear something with difficulty; or to understand something; or to claim something.
ex: I could barely make out the sign in the fog.
在濃霧中我幾乎看不清路牌。

en: To take someone's place temporarily or do their job.
ex: Can you stand in for me at the meeting?
你能代替我出席會議嗎？

en: To reduce the amount of something, especially money; or to cut a plant short.
ex: The company had to cut back its staff.
公司不得不裁減員工。

en: To not include someone or something; or to forget to put something in.
ex: Don't leave out any important details.
不要遺漏任何重要細節。

en: To think about something you very much want to happen; or to imagine something in your sleep.
ex: She dreams of traveling around the world.
她夢想環遊世界。

en: To stop for a moment to rest and breathe; or to stop breathing suddenly because of surprise.
ex: I need to stop and catch my breath.
我需要停下來喘口氣。

en: To die; or to end or disappear; or (of time) to go by.
ex: His grandfather passed away last year.
他的祖父去年去世了。

en: To establish a business or organization; or to prepare equipment for use; or to arrange something.
ex: They set up a small company last year.
他們去年成立了一家小公司。

en: To step onto a bus, train or plane; or to be friendly with someone; or to make progress.
ex: We got on the train at the last minute.
我們在最後一刻上了火車。

en: To meet someone or find something by chance; or to run across a surface.
ex: I ran across an old friend at the airport.
我在機場偶遇一位老朋友。

en: To give control or ownership of something to someone else; or to turn something so that the other side is facing up.
ex: The suspect was turned over to the police.
嫌犯被移交給警方。

en: To prepare a document, plan or contract; or to move a vehicle closer and stop.
ex: The lawyer drew up a contract for both sides.
律師為雙方起草了合約。

en: To stop disturbing or bothering someone or something; or to stop touching something.
ex: Leave the dog alone; he's sleeping.
別去打擾那隻狗，牠在睡覺。

en: To refuse to help or support someone; or to ignore someone on purpose.
ph: turn one's back on the past
col: turn his back on the offer
ex: He turned his back on his old friends.
他背棄了老朋友。

en: To manage without something; or to not have something that you need.
ex: The family often went without food.
這家人常常沒有食物可吃。

en: To investigate or examine something carefully.
ex: The police are looking into the robbery.
警方正在調查這起搶案。

en: To have enough money or food to stay alive; or to feed on something as a main food; or to continue to exist.
ex: Pandas live on bamboo.
大貓熊以竹子為食。

en: To happen or appear; or to move closer; or to be mentioned in a discussion.
ex: Something urgent has come up at work.
工作上出了件緊急的事。

en: To stay away from something or to prevent someone from going near.
ex: Please keep off the grass.
請勿踐踏草坪。

en: To suddenly appear or happen; or to begin to operate.
ex: A new idea started up in his mind.
他腦中突然冒出一個新點子。
